# "Rerun with the merged model when confidence is low" — offline simulation (2026-10-09, zero GPU)

**Scope: ITEM-level rerun only** (whole answer regenerated by the donor). This is exactly simulable from saved runs,
because a rerun = the donor's own output on that prompt (up to T=0.1 sampling noise). It does **not** test the
**online** version (switch to the donor mid-decoding once host confidence drops; the canvas then differs and every
later prediction changes) — that needs GPU, see RETRY_SELECTIVE.md.
Signals tried: mean log-prob, 10th percentile, min, mean entropy, max entropy (raw softmax, not saturated: token
p10 = 0.29). All five give CV accuracy ≤ the better single model.

![](confidence_rerun_sim.png)

Script `../../details/draft_scripts/confidence_rerun_sim.py`; numbers `confidence_rerun_sim.json`.
Host confidence = mean log-prob of the committed non-EOS tokens, from saved trajectories (also tried the 10th percentile).
Rerun the r% least-confident items with the donor. Baselines: random rerun at the same r (1000 draws), oracle.
Threshold chosen honestly by 2-fold CV over r (pick r on one half, score on the other).

| pair | host | donor | oracle | best r (peeking) | random at that r | CV (no peeking) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| IFEval (1.0,0.7) → (1.0,1.1) | 67.8 | 72.1 | 79.3 | 95%: 72.5 | 71.9 (p=0.11) | 72.1 = donor |
| IFEval (1.0,1.1) → (1.0,1.4) | 72.1 | 67.8 | 78.0 | 5%: 72.3 | 71.9 (p=0.22) | 71.8 < host |
| IFEval (1.0,1.1) → (1.0,1.6) | 72.1 | 66.2 | 78.4 | 15%: 72.3 | 71.2 (p=0.08) | 71.9 < host |
| MATH-500 (0.9,0.0) → (0.9,1.1) | 39.6 | 51.0 | 59.4 | 100% = donor | — | 50.8 |
| MATH-500 (0.95,0.55) → (0.9,1.1) | 48.6 | 51.0 | 60.8 | 100% = donor | — | 49.7 |

**Verdict: token confidence carries ~no information about which model will be right.** The router never beats a
random router significantly and, without peeking, never beats the better single model. Oracle headroom (+6–10) is real
but this signal cannot reach it. Contrast: the *finish* signal (no `\boxed` within budget) did work on MATH-500
(CASCADE_IDEA.md: 53.8–54.4 vs 51.0) because it detects a concrete failure, not a soft uncertainty.
